title: Kinetic isolation of the anchored nested commutator
question: Can the zero-time coordinate-resolvent anchor remove every position-only potential from its first nonzero nested commutator, leaving only a kinetic target suitable for a phase-local graph-norm estimate?
method: Rebuild T and V term-by-term for every actual bond prefix on the V=2 edge and V=4 square, in forward and reverse order.
For every translated coordinate resolvent and adjoint, check [V,A_z]=0, [B,A_z]=0, [H,A_z]=[T,A_z], and [B,[H,A_z]]=[B,[T,A_z]].
Scale the coordinate potential by 0, 1 and 2 and check that the nested coefficient is unchanged in operator norm and two-sided Gibbs-weighted norm.
Run a non-importing independent reconstruction, inject a same-site momentum mutation into V as a hostile control, and compile Lean R387 for the abstract ring implications.
Keep the kinetic graph-norm/BKM estimate, shell summability, all uniformities, domain, Cook/common-alpha and every QFT promotion flag open.
finding: The primary lane passes 1019/1019 assertions and the non-importing independent lane passes 1012/1012. The integrated verifier passes 46/46 and Lean R387 compiles. The grid contains 288 beta-weighted contexts, 144 seed rows and 10 bond prefixes. Primary maxima are 7.415006673014076e-16 for [V,A_z], 2.317703490729531e-16 for [B,A_z], 1.0801915330073514e-15 for [H,A_z]-[T,A_z], 1.5436854843327511e-15 for the nested isolation, 1.984473368162697e-15 for potential-scale invariance and 7.402251795272793e-16 for the weighted isolation. The independent maximum-field difference is 7.95529426326475e-18. A hostile V -> V+(1/4)p_left mutation has minimum inner-isolation residual 0.279128784747792 and minimum nested residual 0.364793624984, above the 1.0e-7 threshold.
decision_reason: R-387 adds a distinct algebraic simplification to the anchored route: because all Q3 onsite and bond potentials are coordinate polynomials, the first nonzero coordinate-resolvent coefficient depends only on the quadratic kinetic part. The finite result is independently reproducible, potential-scale stable and hostile-tested. It does not bound the remaining kinetic commutator, its modular companion or any unbounded or thermodynamic limit.

adversarial_review.check: The kinetic and coordinate parts are rebuilt for every actual bond prefix and both term orders; no full-H surrogate is used.
All translated sites, nonzero resolvent parameters and adjoint seeds are tested; the momentum mutation is required to break the hypothesis.
The coefficient is tested at three potential scales, including zero and doubled potential, rather than at a single parameter point.
The cancellation is checked only for bounded oscillator matrices and does not establish a canonical commutation or form-domain limit.
Only the anchored first nonzero nested coefficient is isolated; higher time coefficients can reintroduce V and are not bounded here.
Kinetic BKM/graph-norm control, shell summability, all uniformities, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain false.

next_action: Derive an explicit invariant resolvent/form-core bound for [B,[T,A_z]] and its modular companion, tracking the boundary shell and source. If the kinetic coefficients are summable uniformly in cutoff, volume and shape, feed them into the anchored Cook integral; otherwise register the precise route-specific obstruction. Separately inspect higher time coefficients for the first re-entry of V.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite kinetic-isolation checkpoint only. It proves no kinetic BKM estimate, no shell summability, no domain embedding, no direct Cook/common-alpha convergence, no OS/KMS/GNS dynamics, no gap, no continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A.
no_overclaim: The finite algebra removes coordinate potentials from one anchored coefficient; it is not a uniform estimate and does not imply that the full relative dynamics is kinetic-only.
